title: The built client bundles, by page
headline: Shoppers' pages are lean and the admin is where the weight is: a store page's first scripts are 680 to 778 thousand bytes, about 447 thousand of them React and Next, while the 432 signed-in admin routes have a median of 1,155,530 bytes and every one carries Supabase's client (253 KB) and zod (114 KB) before it is used. Seven small import changes (BN-1, BN-3, BN-4, BN-5, BN-7, BN-14, BN-2) take the admin's median to about 604 KB in a simulation on the built chunks, 13 preview screens from 3.2 MB to 0.8 to 1.4 MB, one Work screen from 4.27 MB to about 1.4 MB, and stop Kaizena Flow's front page from downloading 437 KB of admin scripts it cannot use; routes over 1.3 MB fall from 90 to about 26, the builder's own. This pass added three things the report missed: the previews that load the whole builder, the AI manager's chat script (496 KB, about 95% of it three tables read for two labels) and a store's recommending grid, which downloads 650 KB (204 KB gzip) of zod, the page model and all four languages into a shopper's page. Nothing here argues from a feature being unused: each figure is bytes an owner or a shopper downloads and parses per page load, the cuts move imports and remove no feature, and before opening is the cheapest time to make them; one check over all 560 routes after each build (BN-11) keeps them.

clean: No route outside /admin has zod, Supabase's client, the rich text editor, the builder's English or a whole storefront language in its first scripts: searched by marker string in the first-load chunks of all 560 routes (markers.mjs). The rule in docs/performance.md and storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts holds for first scripts; BN-16 is about a script fetched later.

Chunks carry almost no passengers: on the store home, product page, cart, category, admin home, product editor, pages list and builder, 4 to 11 KB of the modules in a route's first-load chunks are not reachable from that route's own client roots (sim.mjs). What a page loads is what its server modules import, so the cuts are import cuts.

The store home's own share is small: its 35 client roots add 20 KB at most each (site forms 19.8 KB, the header's moving parts 17.7, the buyer switch 15.0, the filter dialog 11.8), and the forms are in first scripts by a tested rule (docs/performance.md: what is pressed before a part's script runs is lost).

The heavy optional parts are separate files no route lists first: the 3D viewer (06bnvraa8v5pm.js, 1.05 MB), the video compressor (3ioq0_ppuc4fl.js, 562 KB) and the CSS code editor (3ek9gab7cmp8l.js, 383 KB), each identified by its text.

The admin frame's own parts are light once BN-1, BN-3 and BN-4 are done: the menus, rail, trail, tooltips, colour and scheme sync, the AI manager's launcher (14 KB) and the storefront header's moving parts the frame reuses (17.7 KB) together are about 64 KB by what leaves when each is dropped.

The public site is even: 23 routes at 673,899 bytes, its form pages (status, report, cookies, get-domain) at 684,680 to 685,386, sign-up at 694,279, the docs at 525,643 and the bare pages (passport, SMS, supply, theme preview) at 479,303; the admin's sign-in, forgot-password, two-step and sandbox start pages are 500,765 to 513,540, close to the 447,102-byte floor.

The admin's English is fetched per area (D540) and the AI manager's chat only when its panel opens (ai-manager-launcher.tsx:32); the storefront's inline editors load only for a signed-in person who turns them on (page-edit-link.tsx). BN-15 is about what the chat's script holds, not about when it loads.

Scripts and styles are served immutable for a year (routes.json cacheControl), so a returning person downloads a chunk again only when a deploy changed it; what repeats on every full page load is parsing and running.

Recommendations are off for a new store (DEFAULT_SETTINGS.enabled is false, src/lib/recommendations.ts:45) and the grid's view loads only after the store's recommendations answer: BN-16's cost follows use; what is wrong is its size.
No finding of this dimension proposes retiring, hiding or merging a feature, and none rests on a table being empty or a feature being unused before opening.

findings.title: Every signed-in admin screen loads the whole Supabase client in its first scripts, for a session listener and for uploads nobody has pressed yet
findings.evidence: Chunk 2du16ociar189.js (179,419 bytes, 44,326 gzip: supabase-js, auth-js, storage, postgrest, @supabase/ssr and env.ts merged) and 2i4juo9spco86.js (57,349 / 16,588: realtime) are in the first-load list of 432 of 560 routes, and no route outside /admin (marker 'GoTrueClient'). The verified report measured 13% and 12% of them run on the admin home. Ten files import @/lib/supabase/client (rg). session.tsx is drawn by the gated layout on every screen; SessionKeeper only calls createClient().auth.onAuthStateChange(() => {}) inside an effect (line 22). The other nine call createClient().storage.from(bucket).uploadToSignedUrl(...) inside an async handler, after a server action has answered (lines above). client.ts imports publicEnv from env.ts, which imports zod to check two strings. Simulated on the built chunks: cutting every static import of the Supabase module removes 259,150 to 259,187 module bytes from each of the 432 routes (the client, realtime and Next's 22.7 KB buffer polyfill); the session's import alone does it on 349, and on 83 the upload and import files keep it.
findings.cost: 253 KB raw (about 61 KB gzip for the two chunks) in the first scripts of 432 routes, of which about 87% does not run there. Downloaded once per browser until the files change; parsed on every full page load.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on each admin screen (today the team; every owner once the platform opens), and a visitor of Kaizena Flow's front page through BN-2.
fix_steps: 1. New file src/lib/public-env.ts with publicEnv() and the type PublicEnv written without zod: the URL is good when new URL(value) does not throw, the key when it is a non-empty string; the same error text ('Invalid or missing environment: NAME, NAME', URL first); the default source stays the two literal process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY reads, so Next inlines them. In src/lib/env.ts delete the zod version (lines 3 to 27) and add export { publicEnv, type PublicEnv } from './public-env', so the eight server importers and env.test.ts do not change. src/lib/supabase/client.ts line 3 imports from '@/lib/public-env'. Without this step the lazy client below drags zod (116,870 bytes) with it.

2. New file src/lib/supabase/signed-upload.ts: export async function uploadToSignedUrl(bucket, path, token, file, options) { const { createClient } = await import('./client'); return createClient().storage.from(bucket).uploadToSignedUrl(path, token, file, options); }. It returns what the SDK returns, so each caller's handling of error stays as it is.

3. In the nine upload and import files replace the static import of createClient and the call with the helper: product-editor.tsx (75, 2324), video-upload.tsx (6, 127: call the helper inside the putWithRetry callback), media-compress.ts (3, 60), product-media-tools.tsx (10, 220), field-file-upload.ts (2, 25), customer-import-flow.tsx (13, 62), data/import-flow.tsx (11, 64), inventory/stock-import-flow.tsx (13, 65), redirects/redirect-import-flow.tsx (13, 67).

6. docs/rules/admin/platform.md lines 50 to 51 (SessionKeeper refreshes tokens in the browser): add that its client is loaded after the page is idle and that uploads load it on the press. docs/performance.md, The admin as people use it: the new figures. On a plain screen the same bytes still load after the page is idle, to refresh the token; they leave for good only on screens that neither keep a session open nor upload, which is none, so this is first-paint work moved, not bytes removed. The token refresh starts a second or two after the page; a token that expires in that gap, or a refresh script that fails to load, ends at SessionRecovery, which refreshes and reloads or goes to sign-in, as today. Two later steps would remove bytes instead of moving them, neither proposed now: (a) uploadToSignedUrl is one PUT to the project's storage address with the token, so the nine uploads could use a hand-written fetch of about 30 lines and never load the SDK; (b) keeping the session with @supabase/auth-js alone, or refreshing the cookie on the server, would take the client off plain screens entirely, but @supabase/ssr's cookie format would have to be matched by hand, and a server refresh changes the written rule at docs/rules/admin/platform.md:50. Measure after step 4 before deciding.

findings.title: A store page with a recommending grid downloads 650 KB more script once recommendations answer: zod, the page model and all four languages
findings.evidence: A product grid that recommends (D139) is drawn by the server and, where the store's recommendations are on, wrapped in RecommendedGrid (content-grid-section.tsx:141 to 145). In the browser it asks /api/recommendations and, on any good answer, draws the shopper's own products with ContentGridView, loaded by import('./content-grid') (recommended-grid.tsx:16 and 133). content-grid.tsx has no 'use client' line: it is the server's view, and it imports t from lib/i18n (line 9, used at 63), three helpers from lib/page-content (line 12) and lib/part-css, which reaches lib/theme-elements and zod (part-css.ts:33, theme-elements.ts:22). In the build, all 56 store routes point at one copy of the grid's script (3-461jjwuauv9.js), whose loader for that import names seven chunks: 649,561 bytes raw, 203,834 gzip, among them 1u2592k6jkhim.js (all four storefront languages, 318,693 / 102,965), 1-5xy7dnrat0_.js (zod, 116,870 / 32,660) and 3553h5joaqwch.js (the page model, 74,836 / 21,199). A store home's own first scripts are 680,264 bytes. The written rules say no zod, no page model and no whole language in a visitor's scripts (docs/performance.md lines 34 to 37 and 52 to 62); the scan that holds them walks static imports only and says so (storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts line 10: 'the recommended grid's, which this walk does not follow'), and the end-to-end check for a whole language opens the demo store's front page only (performance.spec.ts line 61 on). Recommendations are off for a new store (recommendations.ts:45), so this is paid only where the feature is used; what is wrong is its size, not that it loads.
findings.cost: 650 KB raw / 204 KB gzip of script on a shopper's first view of a page with a recommending grid, nearly as much again as the page's own 680 KB / 239 KB gzip; the files are cached after that, and on every such page view they are parsed and run after load on the phone's main thread (zod builds the page model's schemas at import). 79% of it is the three files a grid of product tiles has no use for.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser in every store that turns Recommendations on, on each page with such a grid (a product page's 'goes well with' is the usual place). Nothing today; it grows with each store that uses the feature.
